artifacts.summary: Confirms the task's premise is now stale (an earlier task already re-baselined eager_load.baseline_bytes to 65950, currently passing at 65889 measured); identifies a NEW post-dating regression (skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md now 21318 B over its 20000 B ceiling, caused by an unrelated concurrently-landed commit); confirms deploy-headless.sh's exit-3 semantics are already correctly consumed by command-gate-out.sh (no code change needed for that item); and flags that commands/orchestrate.md remains over ceiling by more than previously recorded.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.note field is used as living, dated justification text (not just data) when baseline_bytes is deliberately re-derived -- e.g. 'Deliberately bumped from X to Y (date, reason)'. This pattern makes a later research pass able to confirm a re-baseline was already deliberate/reviewed just by reading the config, instead of needing to re-derive the decision. Worth reusing for any other config file that records a deliberately-moved ceiling.

deploy-headless.sh distinguishes a landed-but-verify-red deploy (RESULT=landed_verify_red, exit 3) from a not-landed deploy (exit 1/2) so that command-gate-out.sh's postflight completion-deploy gate can run a baseline-relative pre-existing-vs-new-findings comparison (deploy_findings_snapshot / deploy_baseline_new_findings) instead of treating every gate-20-red deploy as a failure. When investigating 'deploy always exits non-zero' reports, check this exit-code contract before assuming a bug -- it is often already correctly handled by the consumer.
